question: Should agent-transcript automatically discover and sanitize GitHub Copilot sessions from ~/.copilot/session-state, or should that source require explicit opt-in?
rationale: The implementation can be technically coherent while still changing the project’s acceptable local-data collection and public-disclosure boundary; that policy cannot be inferred safely from tests alone.

options.title: Approve with final proof
options.body: Treat Copilot sessions as a supported local source after a maintainer approves the boundary and the contributor posts redacted final-head discovery and sanitizer output.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep Copilot support but require an explicit user selection before scanning its session-state directory, reducing unexpected local-data collection.

recommendation.title: Approve with final proof
recommendation.body: Treat Copilot sessions as a supported local source after a maintainer approves the boundary and the contributor posts redacted final-head discovery and sanitizer output.

likelyOwner.reason: Likely repository-level owner for the privacy and product-boundary choice, though local history attribution was not available with high confidence.
